findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` leaves offset unclamped whenever `cursor.is_prev` is true, so ANY authenticated user who can hit ANY BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator-backed endpoint (no `optimized_pagination`/`enable_advanced` gate required) can send `?cursor=0:-999:1` and reach `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start, contradicting the "privileged-only" framing of this feature and the accompanying "this is safe" comment.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor()/math.ceil() directly on the raw `datetime` field value (no timestamp conversion like DateTimePaginator does), which raises TypeError ("must be real number, not datetime.datetime") whenever build_cursor runs for this endpoint's `order_by="-datetime"` results — confirmed via direct repro — so any authorized caller using the new `optimized_pagination=true` feature gets a 500 instead of a paginated response.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — When enable_advanced_features=True and cursor.offset<0, `queryset[start_offset:stop]` slices with a negative start; confirmed against real Django QuerySet.__getitem__ source, which raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`, so every request that exercises the new "negative offset" feature (the PR's stated purpose) crashes with a 500 instead of paginating.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — The enable_advanced_features negative-offset branch feeds a fully user-controlled cursor.offset (parsed verbatim from the `cursor` query param in Cursor.from_string) into queryset[start_offset:stop]; resolving a negative start on an ordered queryset has no bounded SQL LIMIT/OFFSET equivalent, so even setting the crash risk aside, making this path actually run would require materializing/evaluating the whole ordered audit-log queryset, turning a bounded paginated query into a full-table fetch.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator.get_result (used by every cursor-paginated endpoint, not just admin-gated ones) now leaves `offset` unclamped whenever `cursor.is_prev` is true, and `Cursor.from_string` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:53) applies no bounds check, so any caller can submit a crafted `cursor` query param (e.g. "0:-5:1") to force a negative Django queryset slice, which Django rejects with an exception, causing an unhandled 500/DoS on any endpoint using this paginator.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The advanced-pagination authorization gate relies on `organization_context.member.has_global_access`, an attribute with no other reference anywhere in the codebase (grepped repo-wide), so its existence/semantics on the Member/RpcOrganizationMember model cannot be verified in this checkout; if it does not exist this fails closed (AttributeError/500) rather than granting access, but it indicates the gate was not validated against the actual model.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — The new `enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0` branch in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` slices the Django queryset with a negative start index (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`), which Django raises an AssertionError for ("Negative indexing is not supported"), and `cursor.offset` is parsed directly from the client-supplied cursor string (`Cursor.from_string` in src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:59) with no lower-bound validation; this crash path has zero test coverage anywhere in the repo/diff.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — No test exists (or was added) covering the new `optimized_pagination=true` + `enable_advanced` (superuser/global-access) branch of `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, so neither the routing to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` nor the reachable negative-offset crash it enables is verified before merge.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — There is no authorization test confirming a non-privileged (non-superuser, non-global-access) user who passes `optimized_pagination=true` is denied the new paginator and falls back to `DateTimePaginator`, leaving the access-control gate for the new feature unverified.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removing `start`, `end`, and `statsPeriod` from `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer` silently drops previously-supported date-range filtering (requests with these params now no-op instead of filtering or erroring), with no test asserting or documenting this behavior change.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179 — BasePaginator.get_result`'s offset handling was changed (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), altering slicing behavior for every existing paginator subclass built on `BasePaginator`, yet no test exercises this shared-code-path change to confirm existing pagination (forward/prev, offset=0, boundary cases) still behaves identically.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a branch in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` that can pass a negative `cursor.offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but the finding’s key claim—that this would require materializing the entire ordered queryset and turn pagination into a full-table fetch—is not supported by what’s shown here. In Django, queryset slicing is translated to SQL LIMIT/OFFSET (or may error on negative indices), not implicitly evaluated as a full-table fetch, and the diff does not demonstrate any code path that forces full evaluation prior to slicing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator.get_result (used by every cursor-paginated endpoint, not just admin-gated ones) now leaves `offset` unclamped whenever `cursor.is_prev` is true, and `Cursor.from_string` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:53) applies no bounds check, so any caller can submit a crafted `cursor` query param (e.g. "0:-5:1") to force a negative Django queryset slice, which Django rejects with an exception, causing an unhandled 500/DoS on any endpoint using this paginator.

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the new logic sets `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset` (paginator.py around the changed lines), so when `cursor.is_prev` is true it no longer clamps `offset` to >= 0. Since `Cursor.__init__` now explicitly allows any `int(offset)` with no bounds check (utils/cursors.py change shows no validation), a crafted cursor with a negative offset and `is_prev=1` will lead to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises, which would surface as a 500/DoS on endpoints using this paginator.

The finding’s repo-wide grep claim can’t be verified from the diff alone, so the defect itself isn’t provable here, but the newly introduced reliance on that attribute is diff-grounded and worth addressing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179 — BasePaginator.get_result`'s offset handling was changed (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), altering slicing behavior for every existing paginator subclass built on `BasePaginator`, yet no test exercises this shared-code-path change to confirm existing pagination (forward/prev, offset=0, boundary cases) still behaves identically.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes shared pagination slicing in `BasePaginator.get_result` from `queryset[offset:stop]` to clamping `offset` to `>=0` when `not cursor.is_prev` (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). That is a behavior change in a common code path used by existing paginator subclasses, affecting boundary/offset handling. The PR adds no tests alongside this shared-path change to validate forward/prev pagination and edge cases still behave as intended, which is a concrete review concern grounded in the diff (even if existing tests might exist elsewhere).
